title: LEXAM: Benchmarking Legal Reasoning on 340 Law Exams

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM-as-a-judge systems by comparing the scores they assign to their own generated answers (or answers from models within the same family) against the scores they assign to other models' answers to detect systematic favoritism.

Comparing model reasoning performance and LLM-as-a-judge scoring consistency with human experts across different languages (English versus German) using univariate linear regression and correlation tests.
Assessing model robustness and guessing behavior in multiple-choice questions by permuting the order of answer choices and systematically varying the number of distractors (4, 8, 16, and 32 choices).
